description: Dependency updates, deliberately quiet — the GitLab counterpart of .github/dependabot.yml,
with the same policy behind it. openGym is dependency-light on purpose: the frontend is
React + Router + Zustand, api/ has two runtime dependencies. A default setup would still
open an MR per package per week, which on a solo project means the MRs stop being read —
the opposite of what this is for. So: monthly, everything in an ecosystem grouped into one
MR, and a low cap on open MRs.
Run by the `renovate` job in .gitlab-ci.yml, which fires only on *scheduled* pipelines.

packageRules.description: Frontend routine bumps arrive as one MR. Runtime and build tooling move together anyway (a Vite bump usually wants its plugin bumped), and splitting them doubles the review without splitting the risk.

Frontend majors get their own MR. The first grouped run on GitHub bundled a Capacitor 7 → 8 migration in with six siblings, where it read as housekeeping — and CI would have gone green on it, because the test job builds the web app and never touches the mobile flavour. A major that lands alone is at least obviously a decision.

Capacitor 8 needs Node >= 22 and frontend/android + frontend/ios are committed, so a major also means migrating the native projects — Gradle/AGP, the Podfile. That is a deliberate piece of work, not a dependency bump. Drop this rule when you want to do it.
Two dependencies, but one of them verifies passkeys — a major there is worth reading on its own rather than alongside anything else.
Base images in api/Dockerfile and web/Dockerfile.

Odd-numbered Node majors are 'Current', never LTS — they stop getting fixes in about six months. Dependabot's first run offered 22 → 25, which for something other people self-host is a stability downgrade for nothing. Even majors (22 → 24 → 26) are still proposed, which is the move actually worth reviewing.

The images the pipeline itself runs on. Same reasoning as the GitHub-Actions rule this replaces: these jobs publish the container images and build the signed APK, so the blast radius is real — but they move in lockstep and none is worth an MR of its own.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes ignore the monthly schedule and the group — they land immediately, on their own.
